hook: Born enslaved, he led the revolt that created Haiti, the first free Black republic.

pages.x: He was born about 1743 on the Bréda plantation in Saint-Domingue, France's richest colony, now Haiti, where half a million enslaved Africans grew sugar and coffee. He learned to read, worked as a coachman and was freed around 1776.

In August 1791 the enslaved people of the north rose up and burned the plantations: the largest slave revolt in history. Toussaint, nearly 50, joined them, first as a healer who knew herbal medicine, then as a commander who trained a disciplined army.

In 1793 he took the name Louverture, "the opening". One story says a French official exclaimed that this man made an opening everywhere; others think it came from a gap in his teeth. Nobody knows for sure.

When France abolished slavery in 1794, he joined the French side and turned on the Spanish and British armies that had invaded the colony. By 1798 the British, beaten in battle and by disease, had sailed away.

He became governor of the whole island, rebuilt the plantations with paid, though tightly controlled, labour, and in 1801 gave it a constitution that banned slavery for ever and made him governor for life.

In 1802 Napoleon sent a huge army to retake the colony. Toussaint was invited to talks, seized and shipped to France. He said: "In overthrowing me you have cut down only the trunk of the tree of liberty. It will spring up again from the roots, for they are many and deep."

He was locked in Fort de Joux, a freezing fortress in the Jura mountains, and died there in April 1803. Months later his former officer Dessalines defeated the French, and on 1 January 1804 Haiti became independent.
Toussaint led the only slave revolt in history that founded a free nation. Haiti became the first Black republic, and his fight inspired enslaved people and abolitionists everywhere.
pts: Led the largest slave revolt in history
Defeated Spanish, British and French armies
Paved the way for Haiti, the first Black republic
